features.notes: Photo-verified large deck-side glazed door group. Old reference geometry is retained as display_px pending full metric calibration.
Photo-verified tall deck-side glazing adjacent to the door group; renamed from the legacy kitchen_window reference for clarity.
Photo-verified deck-side glazed entrance/slider. Rendered as the measured 1.7m sliding-door portion on the widened entrance wall, aligned with the adjacent exterior wall.
User-measured 740mm opening between the entrance and laundry. Display geometry is centred on the entrance/laundry internal wall and scaled from the current internal-door reference.

Photo-verified narrower internal door from laundry into the toilet. Updated to the measured 588mm width, shifted closer to the west side wall without touching it, with the hinge on the left/west jamb and the swing arc following the door leaf into the toilet.
Photo-verified frosted toilet window. Display geometry is approximate pending exterior side-wall calibration.
Photo-verified hallway continuation toward the entrance/laundry end. Display geometry marks the transitional circulation zone.

Photo-verified standard internal door on the northwest side of Bedroom 2, connecting back to the kitchen/dining circulation edge. Rendered at the measured 810mm internal-door scale and opening into Bedroom 2.

Photo-verified standard internal door between the kitchen/dining area and the narrow entrance/back-entry space. Rendered at the measured 810mm internal-door scale, opening from the entrance into the kitchen/dining side with the swing mirrored from the earlier upper-hinged draft.

Photo-verified doorway between the hallway and lounge. Rendered at the measured 810mm internal-door scale, with the leaf hinged on the lounge-side/east jamb and opening into the lounge. Its display centerline is slightly lowered so the hallway-side edge of the thinner internal wall aligns visually with the adjacent old external wall.

Photo-verified door between the hallway and kitchen/dining area. Its opening lines up with the lounge/kitchen divider wall and is centered vertically within that short wall run. It opens into the hallway, with the open leaf parallel to the hallway's northern wall.
Photo-verified bathroom pocket/sliding door opening off the hallway. Rendered with a pocket-door panel and wall recess marker; exact lateral placement remains approximate until a hallway wall survey.
Photo-verified master bedroom door off the hallway. Door swings into the master bedroom from the lower/south jamb, matching the open door visible against the wardrobe side in master-bedroom photos.

Photo-verified office doorway relationship to the hallway. Opening sits on the right-hand side of the office's hallway wall, leaving the wall continuous to the left. Reduced to a standard internal-door scale based on the hallway and office photos; swing is into the office from the east/right jamb.

current_site.method: External property elements are migrated from the old Matplotlib-005 site sketch only after cross-checking against outside photos. This layer supports external renovation options and shadow/light reasoning.

elements.notes: Overall site boundary from Matplotlib-005 property dimensions. Boundary position is schematic until cadastral/survey data is added.
Satellite/photo-verified main concrete driveway running from the street side along the upper side of the property toward the garage. Replaces the earlier generic path polygon.
Satellite-visible diagonal concrete path from the driveway/front hardscape toward the sunroom/front-house area.

Photo-verified timber deck outside the kitchen/dining double doors and entrance/laundry side of the house. Updated from House-Outline-Internal-walls-deck.png and the 2026-05-14 deck measurement markup. The lower-right notch is scaled from the marked measurements: 0.37m upper return, 0.86m angled step, 2.35m outer side, and 0.51m lower return anchored from the laundry exterior wall. Latest correction lifts the notch so the lower return starts about 1cm below the entrance/laundry front-wall line and sets the top-left house-side deck point 20cm below the dining room external corner. Geometry remains approximate until the full deck perimeter is measured.
Photo-verified small deck/landing at the end of the cottage. Position and size are approximate until measured.

Photo-verified remaining garage/shed at the end of the driveway with visible roller door. Current model places it on the same horizontal line and width as the cottage, with only a small gap to the top boundary.

Satellite/photo-verified larger concrete area in front of the garage/cottage line where the driveway/service area opens out. The house-side edge now meets the timber deck's sloping outer edge, matching photos where the deck steps directly onto concrete rather than grass. Edges are approximate pending direct measurements.
Photo-verified narrow concrete path running along the house-facing side of the cottage and garage, meeting the larger concrete area. This replaces the incorrect broad rear concrete block.

Photo-verified cottage added after the satellite image was taken. The cottage sits to the right of the garage on the same horizontal line and approximate width, replacing part of the old rear garage footprint. Display geometry is approximate until measured or newer aerial imagery is available.
Photo-verified tall hedges/fences along the driveway side and rear/side garden boundaries. These are important shade and privacy constraints.

kitchen_dining.notes: Large openings and deck-side relationship suggest useful daylight, but exact glazing orientation needs calibration.

lounge.notes: Receives borrowed light through sunroom glazing and has a window/opening relationship visible in photos.

sunroom.notes: Extensive glazing and front-lawn outlook make this a primary daylight space; seasonal heat/glare risk should be assessed later.

hallway.notes: Interior circulation space with borrowed light from adjacent rooms.

master_bedroom.notes: Has SW street-facing and NW sunroom-facing windows; exact seasonal gain depends on shading and sunroom geometry.

office.notes: SE window gives likely morning light with reduced afternoon exposure.

bathroom.notes: SE external window; small wet-area window and neighbour-side shading likely limit daylight.

bedroom_2.notes: SE window faces neighbour fence, so morning light is plausible but shading risk is high.

entrance.notes: Glazed deck-side entrance receives daylight but may be shaded by roof/eaves and adjacent walls.

laundry.notes: NE and NW windows should provide better daylight than most service areas, but garage/deck shading needs checking.

toilet.notes: Small service room with limited glazing.
